findings.title: Debug logging left at Error level, dumping full ID lists
findings.body: The cleanup loops call r.log.Error on every batch, with messages like "Annotations to clean by time", "cleaned annotations by time", "Tags to clean" and "cleaned tags". These calls fire even when nothing failed, so normal operation floods the logs with error-level entries. The "ids" field includes the whole ID slice, which can hold up to the batch size (tens of thousands of IDs). This looks like leftover debugging. Remove these calls, or lower them to Debug and drop the full ID list.

findings.title: Cleanup ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The cleanup service interval changes from 10 minutes to 1 minute, but each run still has a 9-minute timeout. All cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, etc.) would now run 10x more often, adding database load and overlapping work. Nothing in the PR description justifies this, so it looks like a leftover from local testing.

findings.title: SQLite inlining decision based on configured batch size, not actual parameter count
findings.body: The choice to inline IDs instead of binding parameters checks r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, not len(ids). This matches today's code paths, but it is fragile coupling. If deleteByIDs is ever called with more IDs than the configured batch size, it will exceed SQLite's 999-variable limit and fail. Basing the check on len(ids) would be correct regardless of configuration.

findings.title: Quadratic string building for inlined IDs
findings.body: The inlined ID list is built with repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v), which copies the growing string on every iteration. With batch sizes around 32767 this is O(n^2) allocation and copying on each batch. Use strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt into a byte slice instead.
